articles.title: 'Don't be spectator, show leadership': EAM Jaishankar to UN on terrorism, global crises
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Sunday urged the United Nations to take a stronger leadership role in tackling global crises, saying
articles.body: NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Sunday urged the United Nations to take a stronger leadership role in tackling global crises, saying it must not remain a spectator to conflicts and other challenges facing the world.Speaking at the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan on the occasion of UN Day, Jaishankar called for reforms in multilateral institutions, arguing that large parts of the world could not be excluded from decision-making.“The UN must show leadership, not be a spectator to global crises,” he said, adding that the case for reformed multilateralism was growing stronger by the day.Jaishankar also described terrorism as a major threat to global peace, rejecting its use as an instrument of statecraft.“Its usage as an instrument of statecraft is simply unacceptable. It can never be justified, it can never be rationalized,” he said, calling for stronger international resolve to counter terrorism in all its forms.The minister said some countries continued to allow political calculations to take precedence over the fight against terrorism, despite the lessons of history.Global South faces '4F crisis'Jaishankar highlighted the challenges confronting developing countries, describing the Global South as facing a “4F crisis” involving finance, fuel, food and fertiliser.He said developed countries also had a stake in finding solutions and called for urgent steps to reduce risks in the international economy and provide nations with more diversified options.“Market distortions through constriction and choke points only add to suffering. A genuine dialogue in this regard is overdue,” he said.Jaishankar calls for inclusive AI developmentOn technological change, Jaishankar said artificial intelligence could transform the world but warned against leaving its development and impact in the hands of a few.“AI promises to be the mother of all change,” he said, arguing that such a far-reaching technology required a responsible, inclusive and human-centric approach.He said India supported a broader perspective on AI, given its universal applicability and potential consequences for societies worldwide.Jaishankar also stressed that progress and prosperity were inseparable, saying the world could not advance while large sections of humanity remained deprived.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Pakistan reopens Iran border after week-long halt to commercial traffic
articles.summary: Pakistan has resumed cross-border trade with Iran through a major border point in Balochistan after a seven-day shutdown disrupted cargo movement, left
articles.body: Pakistan has resumed cross-border trade with Iran through a major border point in Balochistan after a seven-day shutdown disrupted cargo movement, left transporters stranded and raised concerns about LPG availability as winter approaches.Commercial traffic restarted on Saturday at the Gabd-Rimdan crossing in Gwadar district, Dawn reported. Officials permitted the movement of import and export consignments carrying consignment notes issued on or before October 16. according to the news agency PTI.Mir Naveed Jan Kalmati, head of the Gwadar chamber of commerce and industry, confirmed that the crossing, also called Gate 250, was operational again.Kalmati said trucks and other vehicles carrying commercial goods were now permitted to travel in both directions between Pakistan and Iran.Welcoming the reopening, he said it would offer relief to traders and transport operators who had been unable to move their cargo during the closure. The restoration of supplies could also help address Pakistan's LPG shortage and ease pressure on rising food and energy costs.Security concerns preceded reopeningThe crossing was shut on October 17 by Pakistan's commerce ministry, which did not publicly disclose the reason for the suspension. However, security concerns were believed to have prompted the move.The disruption affected LPG supplies at a time when demand for the fuel generally increases during the colder months.The situation worsened on Thursday when unidentified gunmen attacked trucks parked near the Gabd-Rimdan crossing. Dozens of vehicles were reportedly set ablaze, while several others sustained damage.Local authorities reviewed the security situation before allowing trade to resume on Saturday. Additional security personnel have been deployed to safeguard commercial convoys travelling through the area.The reopening also follows a visit to Iran earlier this week by Pakistan Army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir, who held discussions with Iranian leaders on bilateral ties and regional developments.Pakistan and Iran share a 909-km frontier between Iran's Sistan and Baluchestan province and Pakistan's Balochistan province. The border crossings are vital channels for trade and the movement of goods between the neighbouring countries.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: ‘We got them both’: Donald Trump claims US has secured Greenland, Venezuela in ‘greatest real estate deal’
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has claimed that the United States has secured control over Greenland and Venezuela, describing the purported acquisitions as
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has claimed that the United States has secured control over Greenland and Venezuela, describing the purported acquisitions as the “greatest real estate deal in history” during a campaign rally for Republican candidates in Perry, Georgia, on Saturday (local time).However, neither territory has been transferred to US sovereignty.Addressing supporters, Trump claimed Denmark had handed Greenland over to Washington and boasted of US dominance over Venezuela and its oil reserves.“Denmark was so great, they gave us Greenland. You do know that, right? We already have that. We're doing good with that, aren't we?” Trump told the crowd.He also referred to earlier concerns that the US would attempt to take control of the Arctic island.“All of them talked, 'Donald Trump, Donald Trump, he's going to attack! He's going to attack Greenland!' But Denmark gave us—we signed an agreement. You know what? The press hardly covered it. It's going to go down as the greatest real estate deal in history, probably after Venezuela. I think Venezuela. What do you take: Venezuela or Greenland? Both? We got them both!” he said.US-Denmark agreement does not cover GreenlandTrump's remarks came days after the United States and Denmark signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on October 22 to strengthen maritime industrial cooperation and expand US shipbuilding capabilities.However, the agreement explicitly excludes Greenland and the Faroe Islands. Its section on legal status and scope states: “This MoU does not apply to Greenland or the Faroe Islands.”The document also clarifies that it records political intentions rather than constituting an international treaty.It creates no legal rights or obligations and “does not authorise any procurement, award of contracts or transfer of funds between the Participants”. Each country is expected to bear its own costs.Denmark has not transferred sovereignty over Greenland. Although a defence agreement expanded US military rights in the region, it continues to recognise Danish sovereignty and Greenlandic self-determination.Denmark's ministry of foreign affairs highlighted the commercial focus of the maritime agreement in a statement on X, quoting foreign minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen.“Today, Denmark signs an agreement with the US, which paves the way for Danish expertise and solutions in US maritime efforts. The agreement opens significant opportunities for Danish companies and can create new jobs on both sides of the Atlantic,” Rasmussen said.The framework covers three areas: education and training to strengthen the US maritime workforce; equipment, technology and services to modernise shipbuilding, repair and retrofit capabilities; and defence industrial cooperation involving technologies with both civilian and military applications. Commercial contracts are to be finalised separately.Trump highlights Greenland's strategic and energy potentialThe president's claims follow a series of US moves concerning Greenland, an Arctic territory that remains under Danish sovereignty.On October 13, Trump announced on Truth Social that large-scale oil, gas and mineral exploration was preparing to begin in Greenland.The announcement followed a tripartite agreement reached the previous month involving Washington, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Greenland Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen to strengthen Arctic security and defence cooperation.“Massive Oil, Gas, and Mineral Exploration is getting ready to begin in our new and beautiful Greenland!” Trump wrote, adding that the territory's resources and strategic location were important to US and European security.He also argued that Greenland's position would help the United States detect and counter potential threats, including drones and missiles.Venezuela claims follow Maduro's captureTrump's assertion that the United States had also secured Venezuela came after major political and military developments in the South American country earlier this year.In January, US forces carried out an operation that captured former Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores. The couple was detained, transferred to a US naval vessel and flown to New York to face criminal indictments.The operation prompted scrutiny from international legal scholars over potential violations of Venezuelan sovereignty. Trump defended the action, saying the United States had liberated Venezuela from a “very powerful, very nasty dictatorship”.In September, Venezuela's Acting President Delcy Rodríguez addressed the United Nations General Assembly for the first time and signalled a diplomatic reset. She said Venezuela would take “historic responsibility” for guiding the country towards democratic elections and full democracy on its own timeline.Rodríguez also expressed a desire to rebuild relations with Washington.“Venezuela aspires—with the United States, with its neighbours, and with all the countries of our continent and the international community—to rebuild and sustain relations based on cooperation, respect, and equality,” she said.She added that Venezuela was seeking a national “rebirth” after a period marked by internal political tensions, heightened military confrontation with Washington and earthquakes on June 24.Trump announces Audi investment at Georgia rallyTrump's remarks on Greenland and Venezuela came at a rally where he also announced plans for a major automobile manufacturing investment in Georgia.The president said German luxury carmaker Audi, owned by Volkswagen, would invest $4.2 billion in a plant near Macon capable of producing 200,000 vehicles annually.He credited his tariff policies for the decision.Audi chairman Gernot Döllner, who appeared alongside Trump, said the facility would manufacture “our biggest and most premium SUVs”.“This is a long-term investment, because we believe in the American market,” Döllner said.According to Audi's announcement, the plant is expected to create approximately 4,500 jobs, with construction scheduled to begin in 2027 and production planned for the early 2030s.The rally was held as Republicans seek to retain their majorities in Congress ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. Trump has spent October campaigning in Republican-leaning states as the party faces concerns over the president's unpopularity, high living costs and the ongoing war in Iran.Rick Jackson, the Republican candidate for Georgia governor, welcomed the investment announcement, saying: “Thank you on behalf of Georgia for putting the biggest economic deal in Georgia history right here today.”You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2017, Ashton Kutcher and Mila Kunis bought a California beach house for $10.1 million; after mudslides hit the property, they demolished a cottage and began work to nearly double the main house
articles.summary: Ashton Kutcher and Mila Kunis are undertaking a major renovation of their beachfront property in Carpinteria, California, with plans to expand the main
articles.body: Ashton Kutcher and Mila Kunis are undertaking a major renovation of their beachfront property in Carpinteria, California, with plans to expand the main residence, add a swimming pool and reshape the outdoor space. The couple purchased the property for $10.1 million in 2017, and the redevelopment comes more than two years after severe flooding and mudslides affected the surrounding area. Planning documents filed with Santa Barbara County in March 2024 outline the proposed changes, while reporting by Realtor dot com, SFGate and realestate dot com dot au has detailed the property’s history and the scale of the planned redevelopment. Scroll down to read more...A major expansion of the beachfront homeThe renovation plans call for a 2,146-square-foot, two-storey addition to the existing 2,359-square-foot main residence. Once completed, the expanded home is expected to offer approximately 4,505 square feet of living space, nearly doubling its original size. The project also includes the demolition of a separate day cottage that previously stood behind the main house. Plans describe additional outdoor improvements, including a swimming pool, an inset spa, a pool deck, a boardwalk and a trellis, alongside landscaping and exterior lighting.The proposed changes would transform the property from a beachfront home with separate living spaces into a substantially larger residence with expanded indoor and outdoor amenities. The couple’s plans also include merging the two plots associated with the property in coordination with the county surveyor’s office.What happened after the California mudslides?The redevelopment follows severe storms and flooding that affected parts of California between December 2022 and March 2023. In the Carpinteria area, mudslides and rising waterways left properties surrounded by mud and debris. Photographs published in subsequent real estate reports showed extensive muddy conditions around the couple’s beachfront property, including a nearby waterway that had risen significantly.However, it has not been established publicly whether the flooding caused structural damage to the main residence or directly prompted the renovation. The timing of the project, therefore, does not confirm that the expansion was undertaken as a response to the natural disaster. The couple’s plans involve both alterations to the existing house and the removal of the separate cottage, but the available planning information does not establish that the entire main residence needed to be rebuilt because of flood damage.The cottage once offered as an Airbnb stayBefore its planned demolition, the day cottage had a separate history as a holiday rental. In 2023, Kutcher and Kunis partnered with Airbnb to offer a one-night stay at the property, giving a guest an opportunity to experience their coastal retreat. The cottage accommodated up to four guests across two bedrooms and featured a small kitchen, living area and outdoor deck.The listing highlighted the property’s proximity to the beach and views of the Santa Ynez Mountains. The rental was a limited promotional arrangement rather than an indication that the property served as the couple’s primary home. Their main residence is in Beverly Hills, where they previously built a custom-designed home focused on sustainability and a farmhouse-inspired aesthetic. articles.title: A New York mother imprisoned after taking her child without the father's consent faced child-support arrears; an appeals court ordered a fresh review of whether the debt should be capped at $500
articles.summary: A New York woman jailed for kidnapping her own child has been given another chance to challenge the child-support payments she owes.
articles.body: A New York woman jailed for kidnapping her own child has been given another chance to challenge the child-support payments she owes.According to the case details available on Justia, Chelsea Four-Rosenbaum is serving a seven-year prison sentence after taking her child from the family home and keeping the child's whereabouts hidden from the father and police for nearly two months.While in prison, she asked the court to limit her unpaid child-support debt to $500, arguing that her income was too low. On Thursday, a New York appeals court found that the lower court had not properly considered her argument and ordered a fresh hearing. The court now must first find out whether her income during imprisonment was low enough for the limit to apply.Her original child-support payments had been calculated using her earnings before she went to prison, even though she was already behind bars when the order was issued.Chelsea and her husband, Alexander Four-Rosenbaum, have a child born in 2019. Their dispute took a serious turn in 2021, when Chelsea and the child's maternal grandmother took the child from the family home. They kept the child's whereabouts hidden from Alexander and the police for nearly two months. Chelsea was arrested and charged with second-degree kidnapping and endangering the welfare of a child.After her arrest, Alexander filed for divorce and separately sought child support. In 2022, a Family Court ordered Chelsea to pay $408.06 every week towards their child's expenses. The amount was based on her income in 2020, before she was imprisoned.Chelsea was later found guilty of both criminal charges following a jury trial. She received a seven-year prison sentence, followed by five years of supervision after her release.Why Chelsea sought a $500 limitIn 2023, Chelsea returned to court seeking changes to her child-support payments. She argued that she had little income while in prison and could not afford the amount she had originally been ordered to pay.She asked for her future payments to be reduced and also argued that the unpaid amount from previous months should be limited to $500 because her income had remained below the federal poverty guidelines.Under Section 413(1)(g) of the Family Court Act, unpaid child support above $500 cannot build up during periods when a parent's income is at or below the federal poverty guidelines for a single person.Chelsea also pointed out that Alexander had started the child-support case only after she was arrested.Alexander argued that Chelsea had not given a good reason for waiting so long before asking the court to change the amount she owed.In February 2024, the Sullivan County Supreme Court partly agreed with Chelsea. It reduced her future child-support payments to $25 per month, the minimum amount required under the law. However, it refused to limit her existing unpaid payments to $500, saying she had not adequately explained why she waited before seeking relief.Why the appeals court disagreedChelsea challenged the refusal, bringing the dispute before New York's Appellate Division, Third Department. The appeals court found that the lower court had focused on the wrong question. It had treated Chelsea's request as an attempt to cancel child-support payments that she already owed. Under one provision of New York law, courts generally cannot reduce such debt unless the parent can explain why they did not apply for relief earlier.The earlier decision had also considered Chelsea's past work as a litigation attorney, the circumstances of her imprisonment and whether she might receive money or property through the divorce proceedings. The appeals court found that these issues did not answer whether her income qualified her for the $500 limit.Also, although the lower court had accepted that Chelsea's income was below the poverty level when reducing her future payments, it had not established exactly when her income fell below that level or how long it remained there. The $500 limit may apply only to the periods when her income met the conditions set by law.The appeals court has now sent the case back to the Sullivan County Supreme Court. The court must examine Chelsea's income during the months when the unpaid payments accumulated and decide whether the amount needs to be calculated again.You use AI every day. articles.title: After 47 years of marriage, a Kentucky couple divorced but disagreed over selling their jointly owned $703,000 farm; an October 23 appeals court overturned the ruling favouring the husband and ordered a fresh review
articles.summary: A divorce settlement intended to divide a couple’s property has led to a fresh legal battle over a $703,000 Kentucky farm.
articles.body: A divorce settlement intended to divide a couple’s property has led to a fresh legal battle over a $703,000 Kentucky farm. After nearly 47 years of marriage, Mary Holden and Fred Holden agreed to retain equal ownership of the property, but disagreed over when it should be sold. According to the Kentucky Court of Appeals’ October 23, 2026, opinion in Mary Holden (now Carrigan) v. Fred Holden, available on Justia, the court overturned a lower court ruling that favoured Fred’s interpretation of the agreement. The case has been sent back to the family court to determine what the former spouses originally intended.Divorce agreement left the farm’s future uncertainMary and Fred Holden married in 1972 and divorced after approximately 47 years together. In February 2021, they entered into a property settlement agreement that was incorporated into their divorce decree. The agreement covered their jointly owned farm at 3100 Apple Hill Road in Louisville, Kentucky, valued at $703,000. Both former spouses retained 50% ownership interests, with rights of survivorship.The settlement prohibited either party from selling, transferring, renting, mortgaging or otherwise encumbering their interest without the other’s express written consent. It also stated that Fred could continue using the farm, its equipment and tools to raise crops for “at least the next two years, after which the property will be listed for sale.” The net proceeds from the eventual sale were to be divided equally. The disagreement centred on whether the property had to be listed after two years or whether Fred could continue farming indefinitely, delaying the sale for as long as he used the land for agricultural purposes.Wife sought sale after their son moved outAccording to the court opinion, the couple’s son moved out of the farm residence in January 2024. Mary subsequently asked Fred either to purchase her share or agree to list the property for sale. Fred offered $125,000 for her interest. Mary rejected the offer, pointing to an earlier appraisal that valued the farm at substantially more than twice that amount. Fred later declined to negotiate further or agree to put the property on the market.On March 25, 2025, Mary filed a motion asking the Jefferson Family Court to order the farm listed for sale. The following month, she sought summary judgment, arguing that the settlement clearly required the property to be listed after the initial two-year period. Fred disagreed, maintaining that the wording allowed him to continue farming beyond that period. On September 3, 2025, the family court sided with him, concluding that he could continue using the property for as long as he farmed it. The court denied Mary’s request to order a sale, prompting her appeal.Appeals court finds agreement ambiguousThe Kentucky Court of Appeals examined whether the disputed provision was unambiguous, reviewing that legal question independently. It concluded that both parties had reasonable interpretations of the wording. Mary argued that the agreement guaranteed Fred at least two years of farming but separately required the property to be listed for sale after that period. Under her interpretation, he could continue farming while the property was marketed and until a sale was completed.Fred relied on the words “at least” to argue that his right to use the farm extended beyond two years. He also pointed to provisions requiring both parties to share property taxes and insurance in subsequent years, which he said supported continued joint ownership and farming. The appeals court acknowledged that “at least” did not establish a strict two-year limit on Fred’s use. However, that did not automatically mean continued farming could postpone the sale indefinitely.Because the agreement did not expressly explain whether ongoing agricultural use would delay listing the property, the judges found the provision ambiguous. They therefore rejected the lower court’s conclusion that the written agreement conclusively supported Fred’s interpretation.Case returns for a fresh reviewThe appeals court vacated the September 3, 2025, order and sent the dispute back to the Jefferson Family Court for further proceedings. It did not order an immediate sale. The lower court can now consider evidence beyond the written agreement, including the circumstances surrounding its execution, the former spouses’ intentions and their conduct after signing it.That evidence will help determine whether Fred’s continued farming was meant to postpone the sale or whether the property was supposed to be listed after two years regardless of his agricultural use. The ruling leaves the farm’s future unresolved. It highlights how unclear wording in divorce settlements can lead to prolonged disputes, even when ownership shares and the division of sale proceeds are explicitly established.You use AI every day. Once they hold elections, everything will become clear,” Mokama MLA added.Despite his criticism of the party, Singh denied any rift with Nitish Kumar, saying, “There is no distance between me and Nitish-ji; we maintain a cordial relationship. I will go and visit him sometime -- there’s no issue. Let them keep their party; it serves no real purpose anyway.”“I will simply build my own party... I have no regrets. Whatever action has been taken, it’s fine; I have no issues with it,” he said.The JD(U) had accused Anant Singh of repeatedly disobeying the party leadership and using inappropriate and insulting language against its senior leaders.In a further move, the party has approached Bihar Legislative Assembly Speaker Prem Kumar seeking Singh’s disqualification as an MLA under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution, commonly known as the anti-defection law.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Give priority to local artisans’: PM Modi’s festive shopping appeal as Diwali approaches
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday urged people to prioritise products made by local artisans while shopping for festivals, saying their
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday urged people to prioritise products made by local artisans while shopping for festivals, saying their purchases would strengthen the ‘Vocal for Local’ campaign and help realise the vision of a self-reliant India.Addressing the 139th edition of his monthly radio programme Mann Ki Baat, PM Modi said the campaign was helping Indian products reach international markets, citing the export of makhana from Bihar to Greece and arhar dal from Karnataka to the Maldives.The prime minister noted that people typically purchase gifts and other items for their families and loved ones during festivals, and called on them to support local artisans through their shopping choices.“This time too, while shopping, please give priority to products made by local artisans. Your purchases will boost their enthusiasm,” he said.PM Modi said greater participation in the ‘Vocal for Local’ campaign would accelerate the progress towards a self-reliant India.“Therefore, I personally urge you to give priority and prominence to products crafted by local artisans,” he added.PM Modi stresses packaging, highlights traditional skillsThe prime minister also emphasised the importance of packaging in attracting consumers and helping products find a place in the market.“Often, when we see something in the market, good packaging makes us pick it up, and we want to learn more about the product. Understanding this, greater emphasis is now being laid on packaging,” he said.During the broadcast, PM Modi also highlighted efforts to revive traditional skills and farming practices, including an initiative to promote natural cotton cultivation in Punjab’s Malwa region.He said the organisation Kheti Virasat Mission had been working to revive organic farming and had launched an initiative called ‘Nav-Trinjan’ to encourage natural cotton farming.The initiative also started a weaving school a few years ago to pass the traditional skill on to younger generations.“You can imagine how great a help this is for the environment. Friends, a few years ago, 'Nav-Trinjan' also started a weaving school with the goal of passing on the skill of weaving to the new generation,” PM Modi said.Heval river rejuvenation, e-Sanjeevani consultations highlightedPM Modi also spoke about efforts by residents and the local administration in Uttarakhand’s Tehri Garhwal district to revive the Heval river.He said the river’s water level had begun to fall some time ago, while natural water sources in the surrounding areas were drying up. In response, villagers and the administration launched conservation efforts that included rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge and large-scale tree planting.“Today, these efforts have given the Heval river a new lease of life while also helping rejuvenate dozens of natural water sources,” the prime minister said.He also highlighted the use of technology in healthcare through the e-Sanjeevani telemedicine service, which enables people to access medical consultations remotely.“It brings me immense satisfaction to share that nearly 50 crore tele-consultations have been conducted through it so far. This is a massive figure and a prime example of the power of technology, the service-mindedness of our doctors, and the trust of our citizens,” he said.PM Modi added that the service’s extensive network enabled it to reach even the most remote parts of the country, with beneficiaries’ experiences offering examples of its reach.PM calls 12-year journey of Mann Ki Baat a ‘pilgrimage’The Sunday broadcast also marked 12 years of Mann Ki Baat. PM Modi described the programme’s journey as a “pilgrimage”, saying it had allowed him to learn about citizens’ efforts and acknowledge their contributions.“Since then, our journey has been continuing without interruption. You are both fellow travellers and guides on this journey,” he said, recalling that the programme began on Vijayadashami 12 years ago.The prime minister said the broadcast had given him an opportunity to highlight the hard work, courage, dedication and spirit of service shown by ordinary people across the country.“For me, Mann Ki Baat is no less than a pilgrimage to closely learn about the efforts of the people of the country and to bow down to their contributions,” he said.PM Modi added that the programme had brought attention to people whose work might otherwise go unnoticed and had allowed him to connect with families across India.He said he received hundreds of messages from listeners who told him that listening to Mann Ki Baat made them feel as though he were sitting among them and speaking as a member of their family. He described the affection expressed by listeners as an “invaluable asset”.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: India, Australia troops train for coastal, island warfare in AUSTRAHIND 2026
articles.summary: Indian and Australian army troops are conducting joint combat drills across jungle, island and coastal terrain at the Foreign Training Node in
articles.body: Indian and Australian army troops are conducting joint combat drills across jungle, island and coastal terrain at the Foreign Training Node in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, with training activities including combat swimming, ambush drills and drone manoeuvring to strengthen operational coordination and combat readiness between the two armies.According to news agency ANI, the fifth edition of Exercise AUSTRAHIND 2026 is being held from October 19 to November 1. The 14-day exercise brings together troops from the Indian Army’s Garhwal Rifles and Australia’s 13th Infantry Brigade.According to the ministry of defence, approximately 240 personnel are participating in the exercise, with around 120 soldiers each from the Indian Army and the Australian Army.The Indian contingent comprises troops from the Garhwal Rifles and personnel from other arms and services, while Australia is represented by its 13th Brigade. For the first time, an observer delegation from New Zealand is also participating in the exercise.The exercise is being conducted under the theme “Joint Sub-Conventional Operations in Island and Coastal Environment under Chapter VII of the UN Mandate”, according to the ministry of defence.It aims to improve interoperability, joint planning and operational coordination between the two armies, while developing a common understanding of tactics, techniques and procedures for operations in island and coastal terrain.During the exercise, troops are undertaking combat-oriented training under realistic operational conditions, incorporating aerial and maritime dimensions.The drills focus on coordinated operations in coastal and island environments, surveillance and reconnaissance, protection of vital installations, and responses to humanitarian assistance and disaster relief contingencies.The training activities also include physical conditioning, combat swimming, static slithering, ambush drills and drone manoeuvring. These exercises are intended to improve tactical proficiency and combat readiness while allowing personnel from both armies to exchange operational experience and best practices.

articles.title: A Kentucky couple transferred land assessed at $210,000 to their own company for just $1 after a debt dispute; an October 23 appeals court upheld an order allowing the property to be sold to satisfy a $177,668 judgment
articles.summary: A property transfer for just $1 has failed to shield a Kentucky couple’s land from a creditor seeking to recover an unpaid debt.
articles.body: A property transfer for just $1 has failed to shield a Kentucky couple’s land from a creditor seeking to recover an unpaid debt. In an October 23, 2026, opinion, the Kentucky Court of Appeals upheld an order allowing property assessed at approximately $210,000 to be sold to satisfy a judgment of $177,667.88, plus applicable costs and attorney fees. According to the court’s opinion available on Justia, the dispute involved Kimberly A Goodman, David W Hill and their company, Woodsmoke Acres LLC. The ruling followed earlier proceedings that voided the transfer, allowing the credit union to pursue the property despite the change in ownership.How a loan dispute led to a property transferThe dispute began when Members 1st Federal Credit Union filed a complaint against Goodman and Hill in Lewis Circuit Court on July 24, 2024, alleging that they had defaulted on their financial obligations. According to the appellate opinion, the credit union initially claimed $170,073.48 in principal, $32,857.73 in interest and $2,445.26 in late charges. The loan had been secured by a mortgage on property in Pennsylvania. The credit union subsequently acquired the Pennsylvania property through a short sale to reduce its financial loss. Following that transaction, the outstanding debt was reduced to $177,667.88.Goodman and Hill later relocated to Kentucky and purchased property at 3597 Chalk Ridge Road in Vanceburg, Lewis County. They subsequently transferred the property to Woodsmoke Acres LLC, a limited liability company Goodman had formed in May 2023. The transfer was made for $1, although the property was assessed at approximately $210,000 for property tax purposes.The credit union alleged that the transfer was intended to hinder its ability to collect the outstanding debt. It sought to have the transfer set aside or, alternatively, obtain a lien against the property.Court voided the transfer and entered judgmentOn May 19, 2025, the Lewis Circuit Court granted summary judgment in favour of Members 1st Federal Credit Union against Goodman and Hill for $177,667.88, plus costs and attorney fees. The court also voided the transfer of the property to Woodsmoke Acres. A separate default judgment entered on June 6, 2025, voided the company's interest in the property. Goodman and Hill appealed the underlying judgment and attempted to prevent enforcement by submitting a supersedeas bond, which can suspend enforcement while an appeal is pending. However, the circuit court rejected their proposed $30,000 bond as insufficient.With enforcement not suspended, the credit union pursued a further order allowing the Vanceburg property to be sold to recover the outstanding amount. On September 8, 2025, the circuit court ruled that the credit union's judgment liens were valid and superior to other asserted interests in the property. It directed the Master Commissioner to sell the property and apply the proceeds towards the judgment.The couple challenged the order, arguing, among other things, that the bond had been improperly rejected and that enforcement should not have proceeded while their earlier appeal was pending.Why the appeals court upheld the sale orderIn its October 23 opinion, the Kentucky Court of Appeals found no basis to reverse the lower court's decision. The panel noted that it had already upheld the underlying judgment against Goodman and Hill in a separate appeal on May 1, 2026. That decision also affirmed the order setting aside the transfer to Woodsmoke Acres.The court concluded that the couple's arguments about suspending enforcement during the earlier appeal no longer provided a basis for relief. It also addressed arguments concerning Woodsmoke Acres, explaining that the limited liability company was a separate legal entity and that Goodman and Hill could not simply assert claims belonging to the company because they were its members.The judges further noted that the couple's appellate brief did not comply with certain procedural requirements, including providing citations to the record and identifying whether their arguments had been preserved for review. Although the couple represented themselves, they were still required to follow appellate rules. The court therefore considered their arguments under the limited standard for palpable error, which requires an obvious error resulting in manifest injustice. It found no such error and affirmed the September 8, 2025, order permitting the sale.Property can be sold to satisfy the debtThe ruling allows the credit union to proceed with enforcement against the Vanceburg property despite its attempted transfer to the couple's company. The decision illustrates how transferring property to a related business does not necessarily prevent a creditor from pursuing an asset when a court has set aside the transfer and established the creditor's superior rights.The appeals court was not reconsidering the original debt from scratch. Instead, it examined whether the order allowing the property sale should stand. Having found no reversible error, the court affirmed the lower court's order.You use AI every day. articles.title: In the 1850s, gold mining turned Australia's Steiglitz into a booming town with gold-bearing quartz roads; by 1904, only 150 people remained
articles.summary: Gold discoveries in the 1850s transformed Steiglitz in Victoria, Australia, into a thriving mining settlement that attracted workers, businesses and
articles.body: Gold discoveries in the 1850s transformed Steiglitz in Victoria, Australia, into a thriving mining settlement that attracted workers, businesses and families. The town became known for its rich quartz reefs, and its roads were reportedly paved with quartz containing visible gold specks. Steiglitz built hotels, shops, schools and other public buildings as the mining increased. But its wealth was mainly derived from gold mining. As mining activity declined, residents moved away slowly. In 1904, only 150 people remained, deserting a settlement that would one day become a historic park.How did gold turn Steiglitz into a thriving mining townAccording to Victorian Places, gold was discovered around Sutherland Creek in 1854, laying the foundations for Steiglitz's development. The discovery attracted prospectors hoping to find valuable deposits in the surrounding area.A richer quartz reef discovered by miners Hooley and Davis in late 1855 brought further attention to the goldfield. Heritage Victoria's report records that an assay of the reef yielded 72 ounces of gold per ton, encouraging more miners to arrive.Mining progressed quickly and several quartz reefs were found in the area. By 1856 the goldfield was producing significant quantities of gold. The Golden Plains heritage study records a weekly yield of around 1,000 ounces that year, illustrating the importance of the discoveries to the developing settlement.The industry attracted workers with different backgrounds and encouraged the growth of mining operations. By the early 1860s, companies employed many miners, while around 220 Chinese workers were engaged in alluvial mining.Steiglitz was described as a town paved with goldSteiglitz gained a distinctive reputation because gold-bearing quartz was found throughout its mining landscape. The Golden Plains heritage study explains that the town's roads were once made with quartz containing visible specks of gold, leading to its description as a town paved with gold.The phrase reflected the richness of the surrounding goldfield rather than roads made from solid gold. Quartz mining became central to the local economy, and crushing plants processed rock to extract the precious metal.The settlement grew quickly enough to support a range of community institutions. Within a few years of the initial discoveries, it had a courthouse, a Wesleyan chapel and schools associated with several Christian denominations.By the 1860s, Steiglitz had developed beyond a mining camp into an established township. Its population exceeded 1,500 during the gold rush, while 4 hotels, numerous shops, a newspaper and an undertaker served residents and visiting miners.Steiglitz developed a busy social and civic lifeThe town's growth extended beyond mining. A recreation reserve established in 1863 provided space for cricket and football, while a racetrack and tennis club offered additional activities, as recorded by Victorian Places.Steiglitz also gained formal local government status. Its borough council was proclaimed on 27 October 1865, administering an area of approximately 23 square kilometres.However, the mining boom began weakening during the same period. The Golden Plains planning documents describe a downturn in prosperity from 1866, when miners faced growing difficulties and some companies sold their claims at reduced prices.The decline continued into the 1870s. A new courthouse opened in 1875, but falling gold production weakened the town's economy. Victorian Places records that the borough was amalgamated with Meredith Shire in 1879.A second gold rush briefly revived the settlementSteiglitz experienced renewed mining activity during the 1890s, when several mines reopened. This revival sustained the settlement for approximately a decade.The renewed activity also supported local businesses and community organisations. Public Record Office Victoria records that 7 mines were operating in the area during the early 1890s. The Steiglitz Miner began publication in June 1893, reflecting the town's continuing commercial and social life.Mining companies also tried new methods to recover gold from waste left behind by earlier operations. Cyanide-processing plants helped extract gold from mine tailings, but the technology could not reverse the wider decline.Despite the temporary revival, the industry struggled to regain its earlier strength. Mining returns remained insufficient to sustain the settlement's former population and commercial activity.Why did Steiglitz lose most of its residents by 1904The town's dependence on gold left it vulnerable when mining became less profitable. As operations contracted, workers and families gradually left to seek opportunities elsewhere.Heritage Victoria records that Steiglitz's population had fallen to about 150 by 1904. The figure marked a dramatic change from the more than 1,500 residents recorded at the height of the 1860s gold rush.Mining continued in limited forms after the population decline, but it never restored the town's former prosperity. Victorian Places records that the last mine closed in 1941. Some remaining residents turned to activities such as grazing and firewood cutting.Buildings were gradually removed as the community became smaller. The local school eventually closed permanently in 1960, reflecting the long-term decline in the settlement's population.The historic park preserves Steiglitz's gold rush legacyToday, Steiglitz is almost a ghost town, but traces of its mining history remain. Parks Victoria manages the historic park, where visitors can explore the former township and surrounding goldfields.According to Parks Victoria, 2 churches, a former hotel and a small number of houses survive. Signs mark locations where shops and other buildings once stood, while the cemetery provides another reminder of the community that developed around the gold rush. The courthouse, built in 1875, is among the settlement's most important historic structures.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A former army chief, 2 ex-PMs and an Arab party leader: Meet Netanyahu’s main rivals as Israel heads to polls
articles.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu is seeking an unprecedented seventh term as Israel's prime minister as the country prepares to elect members of the 120-seat Knesset on
articles.body: Benjamin Netanyahu is seeking an unprecedented seventh term as Israel's prime minister as the country prepares to elect members of the 120-seat Knesset on October 27.With the vote approaching on Tuesday, the rulong Likud bloc is locked in a close contest with the Yashar party, founded by former army general Gadi Eisenkot, who has emerges as Netanyahu's principal challenger.As Israel heads to the polls, here's a look at Eisenkot and Netanyahu's other challengers.Gadi EisenkotThe former army chief, 66, is the son of Moroccan immigrants and has emerged as Netanyahu’s main rival. A centre-right politician, he founded the Yashar party in 2025 after resigning from Netanyahu’s war cabinet in 2024 and has since been a vocal critic of the prime minister.Also Read | Who is Gadi Eisenkot? Ex-army chief of Israel is Netanyahu's biggest challenger in PM raceEisenkot has vowed to end Hamas’s rule in Gaza within 18 months and opposes the creation of a Palestinian state. He supports Israeli settlements in West Bank but has pledged to crack down on settlers who attack Palestinians.He has also drawn public sympathy after his son Gal and two nephews were killed in combat during the Gaza war. If elected, he would become Israel’s first prime minister of Middle Eastern or North African descent.Naftali BennettA former prime minister himself, Bennett, 54, leads the centre-right Beyahad party, which is polling third. A former tech entrepreneur and son of US immigrants, he rose to prominence in Israel’s nationalist right and settler movement before repositioning himself as a secular centrist.In 2021, he formed an unprecedented coalition spanning the political spectrum, including an Arab party, ending Netanyahu’s 12 consecutive years in power. However, Bennett's government lasted just a year.Bennett is seeking to attract right-wing voters disillusioned with Netanyahu, though he has left open the possibility of including the incumbent prime minister in an opposition-led coalition despite their political rivalry.Yair LapidA former television journalist, Lapid founded the centrist Yesh Atid party in 2012 and quickly emerged as one of Netanyahu’s leading opponents. The 62-year-old has served as finance and foreign minister and briefly held the premiership in 2022 under a power-sharing deal with Naftali Bennett, with whom he is once again allied.A staunch secularist, Lapid maintains a strong social media presence and frequently criticises Netanyahu. However, his support remains concentrated among urban and secular voters, limiting his appeal beyond his core base.Avigdor LiebermanLieberman, who was born in Soviet Moldova in 1958, immigrated to Israel in the late 1970s and became a prominent figure in its political scene. A hardline nationalist on security and a staunch secularist, he is the founder of the Yisrael Beiteinu party, initially drawing support from Russian-speaking voters before expanding his base.Once a close ally of Netanyahu, Lieberman is now a vocal critic of the prime minister, whom he has accused of failing on security. He has served as Israel’s foreign, defence and finance minister.Mansour AbbasLeader of the Arab-Israeli Raam party, Abbas is seeking to mobilise Arab voters, who make up about 20% of Israel’s population. A former dentist, Abbas made history in 2021 when Raam became the first Arab party to join an Israeli governing coalition, led by Naftali Bennett.Abbas could again play a pivotal role in coalition-building if opposition parties rely on his lawmakers to keep Netanyahu out of power. He has vowed to mobilise voters against Netanyahu’s government, which he has described as “racist” and “fascist”.Seeking to broaden Raam’s appeal, Abbas has included former police official Yoav Segalovitz, an Israeli Jew, on the party’s candidate list.Yair Golan Golan leads The Democrats, which represents Israel’s mainstream left and incorporates remnants of the Labour Party, which dominated national politics during the country’s first three decades.A former senior military officer, Golan backs a two-state solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and supports liberal social policies, including same-sex marriage and public transport on the Jewish Sabbath.When Hamas attacked Israel on October 7, 2023, Golan volunteered to return to duty and drove into affected areas, personally rescuing people in his car.(With AFP inputs)You use AI every day. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar has warned that the state government will take action against IT companies found to be deliberately sidelining Kannadigas in job opportunities.In a post on X on Sunday, Shivakumar said the government had taken the issue seriously and would not allow the rights, dignity and employment opportunities of Kannadigas to be disregarded."It is disheartening to hear complaints that Kannadigas are being denied job opportunities in Bengaluru's IT companies. The government has taken seriously the issue of native Kannada speakers being sidelined," Shivakumar wrote.Emphasising the state's commitment to protecting local interests, he said, "In Karnataka, the Kannadiga is sovereign. The government will not allow the rights, dignity, and opportunities of Kannadigas to be disregarded for any reason."Shivakumar also highlighted Bengaluru's position as a global technology centre, saying the state took pride in the capabilities and talent of its local workforce. He warned that companies found to be deliberately discriminating against Kannadiga candidates could face government action."If it is found that any private institution has deliberately sidelined Kannadigas, the government will take appropriate action," he said.Reiterating the government's position, Shivakumar added, "As the voice of Kannadiga interests, the government is always committed to responding to their concerns."The warning after a video of a young woman alleging discrimination against Kannada speakers had gone viral on social media. articles.title: Woman who went viral for barefoot run in sari clears home guard test
articles.summary: Viral barefoot sari runner Kavita Kumari clears Ramgarh home guard 1,600m test in 8 minutes; recruitment runs Oct 24–Nov 5 with PET and written tests.
articles.body: Ramgarh: For Kavita Kumari, the race was never just about the finish line. The 32-year-old widow and mother of two crossed it on Sunday in eight minutes, clearing the physical efficiency test for home guard recruitment at Sidhu Kanhu Ground in Ramgarh town.Kavita, from Soso village in Dulmi block, had first drawn attention when a video of her running barefoot in a sari during a practice session went viral. She is now one step closer to the govt job she hopes will secure a more stable future for her children.The qualifying time for women in the 1,600-metre run is 10 minutes. Kavita finished comfortably within the limit. As a widow, she is also eligible for an additional 5% reservation under the women’s category. “I want to serve and become self-reliant for my family and children,” she said after completing the run.Kavita’s journey had already become a talking point in Ramgarh. She has been preparing by running several kilometres every morning. Her circumstances have left little room for formal training or expensive equipment, but not for determination. Her viral run brought her struggle into public view and turned her into a symbol of the aspirations of rural women seeking secure employment.The women’s test for Dulmi block was held on Sunday, a day after the physical test for male candidates. Of the 930 aspirants who applied from the block, more than 900 women turned up at the stadium. The recruitment drive, which began on Oct 24, will continue till Nov 5.The selection process includes the physical efficiency test, a Hindi writing ability test and a technical proficiency test. Tests for men and women candidates are being conducted separately.Officials said the large turnout reflected growing interest among rural women in public service jobs. Candidates arrived early and went through registration, verification and running queues under administrative supervision.“To ensure accurate timing, RFID chips were fixed to the legs of aspirants,” said home guard commandant Nilima Surin.“Another woman came in a sari to take part. Ramgarh deputy commissioner Rituraj provided her a track suit,” Surin added.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. Download the TOI App.
